arxiv-2111-01430.title: CycleGAN with Dual Adversarial Loss for Bone-Conducted Speech Enhancement
arxiv-2111-01430.creator: Qing Pan 1, Teng Gao 1, Jian Zhou 1, Huabin Wang 1, Liang Tao 1, Hon Keung Kwan 2
arxiv-2111-01430.description: Abstract Compared with air-conducted speech, bone-conducted speech has the unique advantage of shielding background noise. Enhancement of bone-conducted speech helps to improve its quality and intelligibility. In this paper, a novel CycleGAN with dual adversarial loss (CycleGAN-DAL) is proposed for bone-conducted speech enhancement.

arxiv-2407-14991.description: Abstract . Background : The use of gray literature (GL) has grown in software engineering research, especially in studies that consider Questions and Answers (Q&A) sites, since software development professionals widely use them. Though snowballing (SB) techniques are standard in systematic literature reviews, little is known about how to apply them to gray literature reviews.

pmc-11748423.title: Semblans: automated assembly and processing of RNA-seq data
pmc-11748423.creator: Miles D Woodcock-Girard, Eric C Bretz, Holly M Robertson, Karolis Ramanauskas, Jarrad T Hampton-Marcell, Joseph F Walker, Yann Ponty
pmc-11748423.description: MotivationRecent advancements in parallel sequencing methods have precipitated a surge in publicly available short-read sequence data. This has encouraged the development of novel computational tools for the de novo assembly of transcriptomes from RNA-seq data. Despite the availability of these tools, performing an end-to-end transcriptome assembly remains a programmatically involved task necessitating familiarity with best practices.

pmc-12422810.creator: Rachel L. Lennon, Jennifer Storm, Rylyn Koger, Elleigh Thompson, Rosie S. Williams, Mark P. Dagleish, Simon A. Babayan, Mariel T. I. ten Doeschate, Nicholas J. Davison, Andrew C. Brownlow
pmc-12422810.description: Assessing long‐term population health is an important feature of wildlife monitoring and is essential for understanding population resilience. Quantitative assessments of health indices are essential for effective monitoring yet they remain a challenge for cetaceans due to their highly mobile and largely cryptic nature.

pmc-12431160.title: Machine Learning for Preoperative Assessment and Postoperative Prediction in Cervical Cancer: Multicenter Retrospective Model Integrating MRI and Clinicopathological Data
pmc-12431160.creator: Shuqi Li, Chenyan Guo, Yufei Fang, Junjun Qiu, He Zhang, Lei Ling, Jie Xu, Xinwei Peng, Chuchu Jiang, Jue Wang, Keqin Hua, Naomi Cahill
pmc-12431160.description: BackgroundMachine learning (ML) has been increasingly applied to cervical cancer (CC) research. However, few studies have combined both clinical parameters and imaging data. At the same time, there remains an urgent need for more robust and accurate preoperative assessment of parametrial invasion and lymph node metastasis, as well as postoperative prognosis prediction.

pmc-12597291.title: Phloretin-loaded selenium nanoparticles for alleviating cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury via inhibition of the cGAS/STING pathway
pmc-12597291.creator: Teng Xiao, Fanghong Wang, Ye Li, Gaoyang Lin, Xiaochen Wu
pmc-12597291.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality, often triggered by nephrotoxic drugs like cisplatin. The cGAS/STING pathway, activated by DNA damage, plays a critical role in cisplatin-induced AKI. This study explores the potential of phloretin-loaded selenium nanoparticles (Phl/HS15-Se) as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity.

pmc-13066792.title: Kynurenine pathway metabolites are increased in inflammatory depression and decrease with omega-3 treatment
pmc-13066792.creator: Jesper Lindahl, Gustav Söderberg Veibäck, Klara Suneson, Wilma Blanking, Johanna Tjernberg, Darya Ståhl, Åsa Wiman, Filip Ventorp, Sophie Erhardt, Daniel Lindqvist
pmc-13066792.description: Activation of the kynurenine pathway (KP) with resulting accumulation of neuroactive metabolites may be a downstream pathophysiological mechanism of inflammatory depression. The aims of this study were to investigate KP metabolites in inflammatory depression compared to non-inflammatory depression and healthy controls, and whether these metabolites change with nutraceutical interventions with potential KP-modulating effects.

pmc-13179144.title: Differential Responsiveness to Exercise and Cognitive Remediation in Physical Health in People With Schizophrenia: Results From the CORTEX‐SP Study
pmc-13179144.creator: Mikel Tous‐Espelosin, Nagore Iriarte‐Yoller, Agurne Sampedro, Iker Lasa‐Sagaseta, Cristóbal Pavon, Natalia Ojeda, Pedro Sanchez, Javier Peña, Sara Maldonado‐Martín
pmc-13179144.description: Non‐pharmacological interventions, such as exercise and cognitive remediation, have been widely investigated in people with schizophrenia (SZ), showing beneficial effects and supporting their role as complementary approaches to pharmacological treatment. Moving towards precision medicine, it is important to consider variability in individual responses.

pmc-13409636.title: Fibrin-Based Biomaterials in Wound Healing and Soft Tissue Regeneration: Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Applications
pmc-13409636.creator: Bogdan Mircea Măciuceanu Zărnescu, Elena-Theodora Moldoveanu, Adelina-Gabriela Niculescu, Alexandru Scafa Udriște, Alexandru Mihai Grumezescu, Sebastian Vâlcea

pmc-13477800.title: Distinct metabolic dependency on BCAA defines cancer stemness and malignancy in human triple-negative breast cancer
pmc-13477800.creator: Kenkyo Matsuura, Ririko Shinonaga, Mizuki Yamamoto, Yoshiki Yamamoto, Hsin Chen, Ayaka Maeno, Kayo Okuda, Haruki Inoue, Sota Imotani, John Glushka, Koji Miki, Yukako Watanabe, Mamoru Takada, Hironori Kaji, Jun-ichiro Inoue, Ayuna Hattori, Hiromi Imamura, Takahiro Ito
pmc-13477800.description: SUMMARYTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective molecularly targeted therapies. Here, we identify branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) metabolism as a selective vulnerability in human TNBC, particularly in the claudin-low subtype. TNBC cells show greater dependence on BCAAs than other breast cancer subtypes, and intracellular BCAA levels are heterogeneous within tumors in vivo.

pmc-13616810.title: Estrogen-associated thrombosis and the road not taken
pmc-13616810.creator: Arielle L Langer
pmc-13616810.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). en deciding between the mutually exclusive paths of time-limited vs indefinite anticoagulation. The authors capitalize on 14 years of data for patients without cancer aged <50 years from the multinational RIETE registry to characterize the initial thrombotic event and its context, as well as to compare recurrence rates among women with estrogen-associated VTE with those for men and women with non–estrogen-associated VTE. Estrogen-associated VTE was defined by exogenous estrogen use and did not include patients in the high estrogen state of pregnancy.

pmc-13644219.creator: Yaoyao Wang, Junyu Liu, Fang Cao, Yuge Wang, Zhisheng Li, Hanyue Zeng, Mengna Zhou, Qingyue He, Weixi Jiang, Yifeng Li, Junxia Yan
